heroHeadline: Kyiv Strikes Resume Hours After Envoy Truce Expires as Trump-Putin Call Yields No Ceasefire; Quintet Makes First-Ever Khartoum Visit; Lebanon-Israel Talks Set to Stall Until October Vote
heroSubtitle: September 9, 2026 — The three-day mutual capital-strike pause arranged around Witkoff and Kushner's first-ever Kyiv visit expired at midnight, and Russia resumed a mass drone-and-missile barrage on Kyiv on Sep 8 (166 drones, 32 cruise missiles per Ukraine's air force), killing at least 5 and wounding roughly 30 — underscoring how little the weekend's 'substantive' shuttle diplomacy changed on the ground. Hours later, Trump and Putin held an hour-long 'extremely frank' call; Kremlin aide Ushakov said Trump pitched the 'enormous benefits' of restored US-Russian trade to speed an end to the war, but Putin held to Russia's demand for full Ukrainian withdrawal from Donetsk, and no ceasefire was agreed. On Sudan, the Quintet (African Union, UN, IGAD, League of Arab States, EU) made its first-ever joint visit to Khartoum on Sep 8, opening three days of direct political consultations with Sudanese parties; UN Personal Envoy Pekka Haavisto joined, calling a negotiated settlement 'the only viable path' to a comprehensive ceasefire. On Lebanon, a Lebanese official said Sep 9 that talks on the disputed Hezbollah-disarmament 'pilot zones' will make no further progress until after Israel's October elections, splitting the process into a Rome political track and a Florida military track.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN, African Union, IGAD, Crisis Group, USIP, PA-X Database, and Tier 1–3 sources across all media poles.
